subject: Animation
title: Killing Your Darlings at Pixar
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Killing Your Darlings at Pixar.

hook.text: Pixar has scrapped entire films deep into production when the story was not working.

buildup.text: Ratatouille lost its original director eight months before release. Pixar rebuilt it from scratch.

discovery.text: Brave and The Good Dinosaur both underwent massive overhauls that cost the studio years and millions.

twist.text: Most studios would ship a flawed film to recoup costs. Pixar chooses to eat the loss and start over.

climax.text: This willingness to restart is expensive but ensures Pixar rarely releases a film it does not believe in.

punchline.text: Pixar would rather lose money than release a bad story.

quiz.question: What does Pixar do when a film's story is not working during production?
options: They release it anyway to avoid financial loss
They scrap and rebuild the film, even deep into production, absorbing the cost
They hand it off to Disney to finish
